steps.message:
There is a bug in this codebase: when an SVG document like the one below is loaded and drawn, the canvas is incorrectly rendered. Change the implementation so loading documents of this form produces the intended render.

```svg
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
<style>
.blue { fill: blue; }
</style>
<style>
.red { fill: red; }
</style>
<circle class="blue" r="45" cx="50" cy="50"></circle>
<circle class="red" r="45" cx="150" cy="50"></circle>
</svg>
```

Actual:

![actual](/app/.harbor_assets/actual.png)

Intended:

![intended](/app/.harbor_assets/intended.png)

Matching shapes should receive the fills declared for their classes in the document styles, including when those rules live in more than one style element, when a shape carries more than one class, and when a fill value references a paint server such as `fill: url(https://example.com/paint.svg#swatch)`.
I'll investigate how this codebase parses and applies SVG `<style>` elements.

steps.message:
## Summary

The bug was in `src/parser/collectSheetRules.ts`, which parses the document's `<style>` elements into a selector→declaration map.

**Root cause (the black circle):** The outer `for` loop iterating over the `<style>` elements used variables `i` and `len`, but the *inner* loop over property/value pairs **reused those same `i`/`len` variables**. After processing the first `<style>` element, `i` was left equal to `len`, so the outer loop immediately terminated. The result: only the first `<style>` (`.blue`) was ever collected — the `.red` rule from the second `<style>` was dropped, leaving the second circle with no fill (rendered black).

**Fix:** Scoped both loops' counters with `let` and gave the inner loop its own variables (`j`/`jlen`) so it no longer clobbers the outer iteration.

**Also fixed (`url()` fills):** Values were parsed via `pair.split(':')` taking `pair[1]`, which truncated any value containing a colon — e.g. `fill: url(https://example.com/paint.svg#swatch)` became just `url(https`. I changed it to split on the *first* colon only (`indexOf(':')` + `slice`), preserving the full paint-server URL.

Multi-class matching and multi-style collection were the two matching behaviors called out; multi-class was already handled correctly in `ruleSelectorTest` (it splits the `class` attribute on spaces and strips each), and it now works because the rules from all style elements are actually collected.

I added `src/parser/collectSheetRules.test.ts` covering both the multiple-`<style>` case and the `url()` paint-server case. All 39 parser node tests pass.

Note: the visual snapshot/browser tests couldn't run here (no Chromium/network available), so I verified against the node (jsdom) test project.
